drug_class: Antiviral medication (CMV antiviral / terminase complex inhibitor)
purpose: Letermovir is used to prevent a viral infection called cytomegalovirus (CMV) in adults who have received a bone marrow or stem cell transplant. CMV is a common virus that usually does not cause problems in healthy people, but can be very serious in people with weakened immune systems. This medicine helps keep that virus from becoming active and causing harm during your recovery.
how_it_works: CMV is a type of herpes virus that needs special tools to copy itself inside your body. Letermovir works by blocking one of those tools — a protein the virus needs to package its genetic material — so the virus cannot make new copies of itself. Think of it like removing a key piece from a machine so it cannot run. Without being able to reproduce, the virus is kept under control.
common_side_effects: Nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, and stomach upset are the most common side effects. Some people also notice swelling in the hands or feet, feeling tired, or a fast or irregular heartbeat. Most of these are manageable, so let your doctor or pharmacist know if anything bothers you.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you take other medications, especially cyclosporine, since letermovir can raise cyclosporine levels in your blood and may require a dose adjustment. It is not recommended during pregnancy, so use reliable birth control while taking it. Let your healthcare team know right away if you notice a very fast, slow, or irregular heartbeat, or unusual swelling.
typical_dosing: The usual adult dose is 480 mg taken once a day, either by mouth (tablet) or by IV infusion in the hospital. If you are also taking cyclosporine, the dose is reduced to 240 mg once daily. It is usually started around the time of your transplant and continued for about 100 days. Try to take it at the same time every day, with or without food.
